newsitem.title: USA: LaserVision laser system approved by FDA.
newsitem.headline: LaserVision laser system approved by FDA.

text.p: Laser Vision Centers Inc said Thursday it had received approval from the Food and Drug Administration for its MobilExcimer laser system.
The company said it will begin deployment of its first mobile system within days. It said it has MobilExcimer units currently in use in Canada and Europe.

Laser Vision said patient acceptance is growing, and its sales in March were up 15 percent over February, which had been the company's best month ever. "We expect this (patient) approval to have an impact on our rate of growth," said John Klobnak, chairman and chief executive.
The excimer laser is a device that allows eye surgeons to correct nearsightedness with an outpatient procedure that usually takes less than a minute, Laser Vision said.

"This approval gives our company the ability to take laser equipment into many markets which were previously not able to support a full-time laser," Klobnak said. "None of our competitors have this ability, and the barriers to entry are very high."

Klobnak said he expected the FDA approval to be a positive development for the entire excimer laser industry as more markets are opened. He said more than 500 ophthalmologists have expressed interest in LaserVision's MobilExcimer system.
The MobilExcimer uses an excimer laser manufactured by Visx Inc. LaserVision said Visx and Summit Technology Inc will receive royalty revenue.
